capabilities: Show a notification with the assigned shortcut when you use the mouse on a button
Show the command name for buttons that have no shortcut, so you can assign one in settings
Display the called command and its hotkey in a notification when pressing a hotkey
Show statistics of your most used commands
disambiguation: Not a hotkey manager; it only displays already assigned shortcuts and does not create or edit them.
extras: The README warns that buttons are not directly associated with commands in Obsidian, so one button press may produce multiple different notifications. The hotkey-press notification must be enabled in settings and is described as useful for presentations.
motivation: Inspired by the Key Promoter X and Presentation Assistant plugins for IntelliJ IDEA.
problem: Obsidian does not reveal which shortcut is assigned to a button while you are using the mouse, so learning hotkeys means looking them up in the settings.

summary: Shows notifications with the keyboard shortcut for an action whenever you trigger it with the mouse, and lists your most used commands.
